items.claim: Both verses of this two-verse oath unit are quoted at byte tier against the refs that carry them, and every apparatus class falling in the span is disclosed with the right type and the right single-witness posture.
items.evidence: Both spliced runs re-collate at byte tier against oshb:Jer.42.5 and oshb:Jer.42.6, and the English renderings paired with them cover the whole of each cited verse in the staged folded text. The three disclosures made at oshb:Jer.42.6 all check against the marked-verse inventory: one ketiv/qere note, with the doublet standing in the verse bytes as an unpointed ketiv followed by its pointed qere; one paseq seg cited count-only, with no intra-verse position asserted; and one setumah, named under its own type and never conflated with petuchah. No mark, paseq seg, or ketiv/qere note falls at the front seam or anywhere else in the span (inventory over oshb:Jer.42.4-oshb:Jer.42.6: 1 marked verse, 1 paseq verse, 1 ketiv/qere verse, all three of them oshb:Jer.42.6), so the disclosure set is complete rather than selective. The closing warrant is byte-true and correctly deferred to rather than claimed: the following verse reads וַיְהִ֕י מִקֵּ֖ץ עֲשֶׂ֣רֶת יָמִ֑ים וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֶֽל יִרְמְיָֽהוּ (oshb:Jer.42.7, byte), so the word-event onset owns that seam and the oath is not asked to carry it. The oath's own words בְּק֣וֹל יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֗ינוּ (oshb:Jer.42.6, byte) are this span's instance of a construction attested in 10 verses book-wide (skeleton sweep: 10 verses, 11 token occurrences), but it does not straddle either seam here against a stronger tier-1 onset, so leaving it unnamed costs this unit nothing. The two heuristic universal-language hits declared for this span are genuine false positives: one is the mandated count-only tier wording on the paseq disclosure, the other a negation scoped to these two verses, and neither is an exclusivity claim needing a sweep.

items.claim: The frame reasoning is byte-correct at the book's one non-initial word-event site (1 of 21), but the English rendering paired with the span's closing verse covers under a third of that verse while the Hebrew splice covers all of it, and the dropped clause is that verse's own obey-the-voice token.
items.evidence: The load-bearing fact is right. The verse reads וַיְהִ֕י מִקֵּ֖ץ עֲשֶׂ֣רֶת יָמִ֑ים וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֶֽל יִרְמְיָֽהוּ (oshb:Jer.42.7, byte), the word-event formula standing only after the same verse's own wait clause, and the digits given for it match the word-event object exactly: 21 verses carry that formula, 20 of them verse-initial, this the single exception. The messenger formula is named on its actual byte form, כֹּֽה אָמַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל (oshb:Jer.42.9, byte), without tsevaot, and is not blended with the fuller stack; the claim that it is the scene's first such formula holds on the bytes: a skeleton scan of oshb:Jer.42.1-oshb:Jer.42.8 returns 0 koh-amar hits over those 8 verses, the chapter's first standing at oshb:Jer.42.9. The mouth is named as the divine word relayed by the prophet, so the frame-ownership requirement is met. The defect is extent, not content: the splice at oshb:Jer.42.13 is the entire verse, but the rendering set beside it runs 31 characters against that verse's 99 in the staged folded text, dropping the conditional frame and the closing clause לְבִלְתִּ֣י שְׁמֹ֔עַ בְּק֖וֹל יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם (oshb:Jer.42.13, byte), i.e. “so that you don’t obey Yahweh your God’s voice,” (web:Jer.42.13). Gloss extent no longer equals splice extent, and the clause that falls out is one of six instances of the obey-the-voice construction inside oshb:Jer.42.6-oshb:Jer.44.23 (skeleton sweep: 10 verses book-wide, 11 token occurrences) — the same cohesion token that the seams at oshb:Jer.43.4 and oshb:Jer.43.7 turn on. The eight heuristic universal-language hits declared for this span are confirmed false positives: the exclusivity sentence carries its own digits in-sentence, and the rest are keyword matches inside renderings or inside mandated tier-posture wording.

items.claim: The voice-shift argument is carried by the bytes at both cited positions, the span's ketiv/qere and segment marks are fully disclosed, and the internal speaker blend is held open instead of being resolved by an unwarranted cut.
items.evidence: The mode shift sits where this span says it does. The opening verse reads דִּבֶּ֨ר יְהוָ֤ה עֲלֵיכֶם֙ שְׁאֵרִ֣ית יְהוּדָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.42.19, byte), a third-person report of what YHWH has spoken, addressed to the remnant, against the first-person divine speech closing the verse before it; and the next verse carries the span's one marked ketiv/qere, כִּ֣י התעתים הִתְעֵיתֶם֮ (oshb:Jer.42.20, byte), the unpointed ketiv standing beside its pointed qere exactly as disclosed and as the inventory records for that verse, with the prophet's own first person entering in the same verse's continuation, אַתֶּ֞ם שְׁלַחְתֶּ֣ם אֹתִ֗י (oshb:Jer.42.20, byte). Naming the shift without cutting at it is the defensible reading: no formula, vocative, or participant change separates the two clauses, and the blend is left open rather than smoothed. Disclosure is complete for oshb:Jer.42.19-oshb:Jer.42.22 — one ketiv/qere note at oshb:Jer.42.20 and one setumah at oshb:Jer.42.22, both named single-witness, and the inventory returns 0 paseq verses over those 4 verses. Classing a unit whose closing verses are spoken in the prophet's own voice under a judgment type is a per-bytes deviation, disclosed once instead of re-argued, which is the sanctioned handling. The closing warrant is byte-true as well: the next verse reads וַיְהִי֩ כְּכַלּ֨וֹת יִרְמְיָ֜הוּ לְדַבֵּ֣ר (oshb:Jer.43.1, byte), a narrated-time clause that genuinely opens the following scene. The four heuristic universal-language hits declared here are false positives: one is the mandated tier-posture wording on the setumah disclosure, the rest ordinary-English matches, none an exclusivity claim needing a sweep.

items.claim: A byte-true clause brackets oshb:Jer.43.1-oshb:Jer.43.7 across this span's own closing seam and goes wholly undisclosed, and the sentence disclosing the segment mark in its opening verse contradicts itself about what that mark does.
items.evidence: This span's last verse ends וְלֹֽא שָׁמַע֩ יוֹחָנָ֨ן בֶּן קָרֵ֜חַ וְכָל שָׂרֵ֧י הַחֲיָלִ֛ים וְכָל הָעָ֖ם בְּק֣וֹל יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.43.4, byte), and oshb:Jer.43.7 ends כִּ֛י לֹ֥א שָׁמְע֖וּ בְּק֣וֹל יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.43.7, byte) — the same negated obedience clause standing on both sides of the cut, framing oshb:Jer.43.1-oshb:Jer.43.7 as one obedience-failure report. That construction is attested in 10 verses book-wide (skeleton sweep: 10 verses, 11 token occurrences), six of them inside this Egypt complex, so its doubling either side of the seam is a cohesion signal and not density noise; nothing in the span names it, and an undisclosed byte-true device straddling a seam argues continuity against the cut. Second, the disclosure sentence for the opening verse asserts in one breath that the mark is a closing setumah and that it falls inside that same verse, and it carries two predicates for one subject; the inventory records a verse-keyed segment close there, so the inside-the-verse half is not sourceable, and the rejected alternative then leans on that same mis-stated shape. The frame distinction drawn here is correct and worth keeping: the opening verse reads וַיְהִי֩ כְּכַלּ֨וֹת יִרְמְיָ֜הוּ לְדַבֵּ֣ר (oshb:Jer.43.1, byte), a narrated-time clause and not the word-event formula, and it is not among the 21 verses that carry that formula. A third, smaller gap: the note claims both name spellings are given as the bytes carry them, but only the accuser's patronymic at oshb:Jer.43.2 is spliced, while the corresponding form at oshb:Jer.42.1 is given in English only — the two are in fact consonantally identical, so the claim is true but unquoted on one side. Of the two heuristic universal-language hits declared for this span, the count-discipline one is a genuine false positive; the disposition on the naming sentence does not fully hold, since that sentence asserts both spellings are given as the bytes carry them while one of the two is never spliced.

items.claim: This span twice describes the following word-event as a dated notice, which its bytes do not carry, and it sits at high confidence on an onset that carries no formula, vocative, or participant change.
items.evidence: The verse in question reads וַיְהִ֤י דְבַר יְהוָה֙ אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ בְּתַחְפַּנְחֵ֖ס לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Jer.43.8, byte): a verse-initial word-event formula with a place adjunct and no year, month, regnal, or ordinal element anywhere in it. It is not among the book's 19 classified date-header candidate sites, and a skeleton scan of the verse returns 0 date tokens; the same verse is described correctly as a plain word-event onset where it is engaged next, so the date wording here is byte-unsupported, and it appears twice — once in the closing warrant and once in the rejected alternative, which makes it the stated ground for declining to carry past this seam. Separately, the calibration sits high on the weaker of the two edges. The onset verse opens וַיִּקַּ֞ח יוֹחָנָ֤ן בֶּן קָרֵ֨חַ֙ וְכָל שָׂרֵ֣י הַחֲיָלִ֔ים (oshb:Jer.43.5, byte) — the same actors already named at oshb:Jer.43.4, a narrative action verb, and no formula, vocative, addressee change, or participant change to mark it — and the negated obedience clause at oshb:Jer.43.4 and oshb:Jer.43.7 brackets oshb:Jer.43.1-oshb:Jer.43.7 across that onset (skeleton sweep: 10 verses book-wide, 11 token occurrences), undisclosed here as well. The other span carried at high confidence nearby is bounded by a word-event formula at both edges, oshb:Jer.43.8 and oshb:Jer.44.1; this one is formula-bound only at its close. That close is sound: oshb:Jer.43.8 does open a fresh word-event, and the setumah at oshb:Jer.43.7 is correctly named single-witness and correctly kept off the driver line.

items.claim: The word-event onset, the fused command-and-interpretation ruling, both ketiv/qere notes, and the closing header are all verified on the bytes, and the divine title inside the span is carried without blending.

The title carried there is the full stack, a member of the object attested in 32 verses (skeleton sweep: 32 verses), and it is not restated as anything else. Disclosure is complete and correct: two ketiv/qere notes, at oshb:Jer.43.10 and oshb:Jer.43.11, each quoted with ketiv and qere kept distinct rather than silently resolved to the qere, matching the inventory counts for those verses; one setumah at the front seam and one at oshb:Jer.43.13; and the inventory returns 0 paseq verses over oshb:Jer.43.8-oshb:Jer.43.13, so nothing is passed over. items.claim: This span treats its second internal messenger formula as a restatement of the same full divine title, but that formula's bytes carry a different and far rarer stack, and the two paseq segs inside the span go undisclosed while all four segment marks are disclosed.
items.evidence: The first movement opens כֹּה אָמַ֞ר יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל (oshb:Jer.44.2, byte) and the concluding sentence carries כֹּֽה אָמַ֞ר יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל (oshb:Jer.44.11, byte); both are members of the full-stack object attested in 32 verses (skeleton sweep: 32 verses). The second movement carries כֹּֽה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָה֩ אֱלֹהֵ֨י צְבָא֜וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל (oshb:Jer.44.7, byte) — an elohei-augmented stack attested in only 3 verses book-wide (skeleton sweep: 3 verses), and not a member of the 32-verse object at all. Calling it a restatement of the full divine title blends two byte-distinct count objects, and it does so where the blend carries weight: the rejected alternative declines a cut at that position on the ground that both internal restatements are mere recurrences of one formula, so the one title stack in this span that is not a member of that 32-verse object is the evidence that argument had to weigh and did not. The distinction is drawn correctly for the shorter and fuller stacks at oshb:Jer.42.9 and oshb:Jer.42.15, so the object discipline is available here and simply not applied. Second, disclosure inside the span is asymmetric: paseq segs stand at oshb:Jer.44.9 and oshb:Jer.44.14 (single-witness inventory, count-only) and neither is named, while all four setumah marks in the same verses are disclosed in full, and the same disclosure object is named at oshb:Jer.42.6 and oshb:Jer.42.16 — so the omission reads as inconsistency rather than a settled posture. The header claim itself is sound: the opening verse reads הַדָּבָר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָיָ֣ה אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ (oshb:Jer.44.1, byte) with the aleph-lamed particle, a genuine member of the 11-verse superscription shape, and the koh-amar census digit cited for the density argument matches the formula's book-wide verse count.
